questions.question: Mia has 36 stickers. She gets 10 more. How many stickers does she have now?
questions.explain: Getting 10 more means adding 10. 36 plus 10 is 46. The trap is adding 1 to the ones digit to get 37.

questions.question: Ben has 72 shells. He gives 10 to his friend. How many does he have left?
questions.explain: Giving away 10 means subtracting 10. 72 minus 10 is 62. The trap is changing the ones digit to get 71.

questions.question: A bus has 28 kids on it. 10 more kids get on at the next stop. How many kids are on the bus now?
questions.explain: 10 more kids means adding 10. 28 plus 10 is 38. The trap is adding 1 to the ones digit to get 29.

questions.question: Sara has 55 marbles. She loses 10. How many marbles does she have now?
questions.explain: Losing 10 means subtracting 10. 55 minus 10 is 45. The trap is changing the ones digit to get 54.

questions.question: Tom has 44 cards. He gets 10 more from his sister, then he gives 10 to his friend. How many cards does Tom have now?
questions.explain: Gaining 10 and giving away 10 cancel each other out, so he still has 44. The trap is only doing one of the two steps and forgetting the other.

questions.question: I am 10 more than 56. I am also 10 less than 76. What number am I?
questions.explain: 10 more than 56 is 66, and 10 less than 76 is also 66. Both clues point to the same answer. The trap is changing the ones digit instead of the tens digit.

questions.question: Jake says: 58 plus 10 is 59. What did Jake do wrong?
options: He subtracted 1 from the tens digit by mistake.
He added 10 to the ones digit, making it 18.
He added 1 to the ones digit instead of 10.
He added 1 to the tens digit instead of the ones.
questions.explain: Jake added 1 to the ones digit (8 to 9) instead of adding 10 to the tens part. 58 plus 10 should be 68.

questions.question: What number is 10 more than 23?
questions.explain: To find 10 more, add 1 to the tens digit. 23 becomes 33. A common trap is to add 1 to the ones digit instead.

questions.question: What number is 10 less than 47?
questions.explain: To find 10 less, subtract 1 from the tens digit. 47 becomes 37. A common trap is to change the ones digit instead.

questions.question: Count by 10s. What comes after 60?
questions.explain: Counting by 10s means adding 10 each time, so after 60 comes 70. A common trap is to count by 1s and land on 69.

questions.question: What number is 10 more than 85?
questions.explain: To find 10 more than 85, add 1 to the tens digit to get 95. A common trap is to change the ones digit or round to 80.

questions.question: Maya has 34 stickers. She gets 10 more. How many stickers does she have now?
questions.explain: Adding 10 means adding 1 to the tens digit, so 34 + 10 = 44. A common trap is to add 1 to the ones digit instead.

questions.question: Leo had 58 marbles. He gave away 10. How many does he have left?
questions.explain: Taking away 10 means subtracting 1 from the tens digit, so 58 - 10 = 48. A common trap is to round to 50 or change the ones digit.

questions.question: Sam is counting by 10s. He says 20, 30, 40, 50. What does he say next?
questions.explain: Counting by 10s, after 50 comes 60. A common trap is to count by 1s and land on 59.

questions.question: A bus has 42 people. 10 more get on. How many are on the bus now?
questions.explain: Adding 10 to 42 gives 52, because you add 1 to the tens digit. A common trap is to add 1 to the ones digit instead.

questions.question: A fish tank has 25 fish. The store adds 10 more, then 10 swim away. How many fish are there now?
questions.explain: Adding 10 and then taking away 10 brings you right back to 25. A common trap is to forget one of the two steps.

questions.question: I think of a number. I add 10 to it and get 63. What is my number?
questions.explain: If adding 10 gives 63, take 10 away to find the starting number: 63 - 10 = 53. A common trap is to change the ones digit instead of the tens.

questions.question: Tom counts by 10s: 10, 20, 30, __, 50, 60. What number is missing?
questions.explain: Between 30 and 50, the next number counting by 10s is 40. A common trap is to count by 1s and land on 39.

questions.question: Ben says 47 + 10 = 48. What did he do wrong?
options: He jumped to the next ten
questions.explain: 47 + 10 = 57, because you add 1 to the tens digit. Ben added 1 to the ones digit instead, which gives 48.
